archetype: Mardu Vampire typal go-wide aggro that kills by trigger rather than by combat: eminence mints a body per Vampire cast, doublers multiply the mint, and entry payoffs turn each arrival into life loss. The aggro frame agrees, and v1.0.0 moved it one step further toward bodies — creatures 33 against the band's 26-32, interaction-breadth down from 4 classes to 3.
verdict: It functions and every multi-card component turns over: 91.3% turn-3 land drop, a castable Vampire in 92.3% of games, lords 79.0%, a draw engine 73.3%. What I can measure end to end is conversion, and that is where it thins — THE GO-WIDE KILL assembles by turn six in 28.5% of games (mean turn 5.043), and its payoff leg is the thinnest of its three legs — six cards at 36.4% of openers against the multiplier's seven and the ignition leg's thirteen. That leg is now declared correctly: the group this document said was wrong in both directions has been split by trigger event, Mirkwood Bats is in it and the two death drains have a component of their own, and the pod attacks the biggest revealed damage dealer in 67.3% of 712 declare-attackers decisions, ci95 [0.637, 0.706] against a uniform 51.5%, permutation p = 0.0001. Card draw is not what costs games: eleven real sources survive an oracle read against a floor of ten. Black may be — 30 sources of 36 and 82.2% on-curve with rocks against a cited 90% — and this document declines to rank it against conversion rather than pretending to, because the instrument that measures assembly cannot see colour at all; that ranking is routed, not decided here.

components.reading: Three replacement doublers and four extra token-makers, 73.5% assembled. Stack 010 proves the doublers stacking to eight tokens off one eminence trigger.

The thinnest of the kill's three legs — six cards, 36.4% of openers, 67.4% assembled and 56.7% by turn six — and it is now declared as such: round 1 read this group as seven cards at 72.9%, which counted two death drains that cannot fire when a token arrives and omitted Mirkwood Bats, and the correction has been applied. Bats is the member that changes magnitude rather than probability: checker-passed stack 011 rules it triggers ONCE PER TOKEN, not once per creation event, so it is the payoff in the 99 that scales with the doublers instead of alongside them.

Blood Artist and Cruel Celebrant, now a component of their own: two cards, 13.7% of openers, 30.4% assembled and 24.1% by turn six. They are a REACHABLE second line rather than an inert pair — the deck can manufacture the death without waiting to be attacked (Skullclamp kills a 1/1 token for {1}; Indulgent Aristocrat's sacrifice outlet carries no tap symbol and no timing restriction) — which is also why a resolved wipe pays the pilot. What they cannot do is fire on the entry event stack 009 kills from, which is why they are not the kill's leg.

The combat kill, 79.0% assembled — and the sim does NOT show combat losing the exchange: the paired per-game difference (taken minus dealt) is +8.60 with a 95% t-interval of [-15.26, +32.46] over 20 AI-vs-AI games, sign reversed or level in 7 of them. What is contested is who the swings are aimed at, which is targeting.json's question, not this one.
73.3% assembled, 62.1% by turn six. Log 001's gas problem was a countered Champion of Dusk, not an absent one — the card was drawn and cast.
60.2% assembled, 48.8% by turn six. Five is the redundancy corpus's 31%-of-openers tier, which is the right size for a deck whose spells cost three.
61.0% assembled, 49.8% by turn six — and it is held rather than deployed, so the practical rate is lower than the goldfish's by whatever the mana was spent on instead.

43.1% assembled, 33.8% by turn six, and flagged thin at three cards. The audit's own closers are Swords to Plowshares and Generous Gift — two of the ten cards just cut — but only ONE of them closes it: Swords exiles a creature and cannot answer a noncreature permanent at all. The role route is coarse there; the card is not.

single_points_of_failure.component: THE SURVIVING INFINITE (stacks 004 and 006): Bloodthirsty Conqueror + a lifegain-loss half
single_points_of_failure.why: One card: 7.1% of opening sevens, 4.6% assembled unassisted and 10.2% with a tutor. That is the declared ceiling on the line, not a defect — and the table has already found it: log 001 has Conqueror as one of the two counterspells that decided the game. The deck has another route, and here is exactly what that route has been proved to do: stack 009 is EXACTLY lethal into a three-opponent pod at 12 life each with zero margin, and it opens on a board that already holds three payoffs and a doubler — Purphoros, Impact Tremors, Warleader's Call and Anointed Procession — five lands, and three opponents holding no instant-speed interaction. Its per-seat figure is 12; the 36 pod total is not interchangeable with it. So what is proved is that the payoff class closes a game with no infinite piece anywhere on the board, which is the claim this entry needs. What is NOT proved is a kill from 40, and engine.json's own third open question is precisely that count. Stack 011 adds a second route on the same terms: Mirkwood Bats triggers once per token created, so the doublers multiply its drain — two doublers and four tokens is four triggers — and that route needs no four-permanent board. Bounded the same way, because 011 bounds itself: it measures 4 per opponent across a TWO-opponent pod, and it says in terms that putting Bats on stack 010's eight-token board is a counterfactual no tracked board shows, with both of 010's opponents at 40. Read the ceiling as declared rather than as a defect on that basis, and no further.

Its Offspring cost also makes a token copy, so it feeds the doublers it is a payoff for. Sized honestly, and the contrast is now checker-passed: Kambal reads 'one or more tokens', so it triggers per EVENT, while stack 011 rules Mirkwood Bats triggers per TOKEN. Kambal buys the leg redundancy — 6 to 8 with Agate Instigator, 36.4% to 45.6% of openers — and buys it no magnitude, and its first ability (copying opponents' tokens) is a metagame bonus that happens to be live against the token seat in the sim pod. THE PAIRING CHANGED THIS ROUND, and the reason is the whole point of the marginal frame: round 1 cut Vampire of the Dire Moon for it, which is a member of the 13-card castable-Vampire group — the THIRD need on THE GO-WIDE KILL, and the leg whose honest modelling took that kill from 0.531 to 0.491 assembled, and to 0.445 once the payoff split landed. That swap moved the payoff leg up (6 -> 7, 36.4% -> 41.2% of openers) and the ignition leg down (13 -> 12, 63.9% -> 60.7%) on the SAME target, and nothing netted the two. Paired against Sanguine Bond instead, no leg of the kill moves down at all — the cost lands on a declared bonus line instead — and priced properly, not with that line's pre-cut rate: THE SURVIVING INFINITE's second group is Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose and Sanguine Bond, and cutting one takes it from two copies to one, 13.7% of opening sevens to 7.1%. The tracked 4.6% assembled and 2.8% by turn six are measured WITH Sanguine Bond in the group and do not describe the deck after this swap; the post-swap rate is unmeasured, and open_questions[0] carries it into the next sandbox. It is still priced as painful where it belongs, in cut_candidates.

open_questions.question: ANSWERED for its first half, still open for its second. The payoff group has been corrected and re-derived: the leg is six creation-and-entry payoffs at 36.4% of openers, 67.4% assembled, 56.7% by turn six; Blood Artist and Cruel Celebrant hold their own component at 13.7% / 30.4% / 24.1%; and THE GO-WIDE KILL moved from 0.491 assembled and 0.327 by turn six to 0.445 and 0.285, mean turn 4.773 to 5.043. What remains unrun is the sandbox with this document's four (add, natural_cut) pairs applied, which is the only way to price two things it cannot derive: the payoff leg at eight copies against the kill's other two legs, and THE SURVIVING INFINITE once Sanguine Bond leaves its second group.
open_questions.why_it_matters: The first half is settled and the answer is on record: every figure this document sized off 0.327 has been re-sized, and the reading it was sized for held — a six-card leg is thinner than a seven-card one, so the payoff half binds harder rather than less. The second half still decides whether the four swaps are worth making as a set, which no figure here can say.

open_questions.question: Mirkwood Bats reads 'whenever you create or sacrifice a token' where Caretaker's Talent reads 'whenever one or more tokens you control enter ... only once each turn'. When one eminence trigger creates eight tokens as a single replaced event (stack 010), does Mirkwood Bats trigger eight times or once?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the difference between 1 and 8 life loss per opponent from one card, and it decides whether the newest payoff scales with the doublers or is a rounding error. It changes the kill's magnitude, not its probability — and it changes how the corrected payoff group should be weighted.

open_questions.question: Does Bloodletter of Aclazotz double DAMAGE as well as stated life loss? Stacks 003 and 007 only ever tested 'each opponent loses N life' from Sanctum Seeker and Throne of the God-Pharaoh; nobody has run Purphoros dealing 2 to each opponent through it.
open_questions.why_it_matters: It decides whether this deck has one engine or two. If damage doubles, the drain doubler and the entry-payoff plan are the same kill and Bloodletter's single point of failure is priced far too low; if it does not, the two plans are genuinely separate and its {1}{B}{B}{B} buys one of them.

open_questions.question: What does the corpus say about typal and uncounterable mana against raw source counts? manabase.land_colors credits Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth and Cavern of Souls ZERO colour sources, so both left the 99 without moving the colour-sources axis by a single point, and no measured axis will move if either comes back.
open_questions.why_it_matters: Of the four axes deck-audit reports under target — colour-sources, ramp, card-advantage, interaction-breadth — two survive an oracle read (colour-sources here, and interaction-breadth, whose two zeros this document confirms card by card), and colour-sources is the mana one. The measure is blind to the two cards most relevant to it. Recon (as_of 2026-08-03) has Cavern of Souls in 40.7% of Tokens-tagged Edgar decks and calls it 'the community's answer to having a key lord countered'; log 001 is one game decided by two counterspells, which is an anecdote and not a rate. Buying a card the axis cannot see is the Bojuka Bog mistake, and refusing one because the axis cannot see it is the same mistake wearing the other face.

open_questions.question: Is the black shortfall costing this deck games, or is conversion? The bench cannot currently answer it: goldfish.py's `_mana_pips` reduces every cost to generic-equivalent mana and its mulligan rule counts lands rather than colours, so assembly rates, the turn-3 land drop and the keep rate are all colour-blind by construction, and mana_analysis's Karsten castability is a static hypergeometric that never meets the deck's curve. What would settle it is a colour-aware run: how often is a black spell in hand, affordable by total mana, and uncastable for want of a black source?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This is the one ranking this diagnosis declines to make, and it decides whether the next slots go to the payoff leg or to the mana base. It is also a gap in the SIMULATOR rather than in this document: no artifact in the repo can currently distinguish 'short on black' from 'short on mana', which is why a 6-source deficit and a 0.822 castability sit here unranked beside a measured conversion rate. Recorded so the next reader inherits the question rather than the guess.

open_questions.question: Does the death-drain line actually convert? It now has a measured rate — Blood Artist and Cruel Celebrant, 30.4% assembled and 24.1% by turn six — and no checker-passed stack showing it closing a game. engine-critic established the deck can manufacture the death rather than wait for it (Skullclamp for {1} on a 1/1 token; Indulgent Aristocrat's outlet has no tap symbol and no timing restriction), so the question is how many deaths a seat costs at what mana, the way stack 009 did for the entry event.
open_questions.why_it_matters: It fell out of the split. The declaration now states this as 'a reachable second line' and the audit reports a rate for it, which means the deck is one stack away from having two proved routes that need no infinite piece instead of one — and that is the argument the single-point-of-failure entry on Bloodthirsty Conqueror rests on. Unproved, it is a rate for a line nobody has shown converting.

gaps: CHANGE RECORD, rounds 2 and 3 — complete, because a record that claims to list what moved and lists half of it is worse than one that claims less. ROUND 2 withdrew three things: (a) the verdict's damage-comparison inference, which read a difference off two overlapping marginal intervals — the reasoning `intervals_overlap` was deleted from sim/experiment.py for — where the paired re-derivation puts zero inside [-15.26, +32.46]; (b) the cut candidate Vampire of the Dire Moon, entirely, because it was a member of the kill's ignition leg and its cost was priced against a card the same list proposed cutting; (c) half of Agate Instigator's stated value, from a misquoted 31-to-41 spread to the true six-to-seven move of 4.8 points. It also RE-POINTED three citations that named the right section and the wrong row of it, none of which the skeptic had asked for: engine.single_points_of_failure[0] and [1] moved off the effect-class row onto 'a named card is 7.1% of your opening seven', which is what a one-card component actually asserts, and lean_into[1] moved onto the tutors row. ROUND 3 withdrew the largest claim in the document: the ranking of conversion above the black shortfall. Two of its three supports could not see colour (goldfish.py:_mana_pips is generic-equivalent; the mulligan rule counts lands) and the third was one logged game, against one colour-aware number pointing the other way. Nothing in the three explain-aways moved in either round: the skeptic re-derived all eleven card-advantage sources, all twelve interaction copies and both interaction-breadth zeros independently and confirmed them, and confirmed that cut_candidates[1]'s bare 41.05 is a real cross-seat finding — Edgar takes the most combat damage in this pod, 41.05 against the winning seat's 14.60.

The deck has ONE logged game. Log 001 is texture on the measurements, never a rate; its two settled questions — Edgar cast at eight mana was piloting, and three wipes with no protection in hand was variance — are treated as settled here and are not re-argued.

RESOLVED, and recorded rather than deleted. Rounds 1 to 3 quoted 0.491 assembled / 0.327 by turn six because that was the figure on disk, while stating that the correction to 0.285 was a claim from the other side of the table and not a measurement this document could make. The correction has since been applied and re-derived, and every site is now carried at 0.445 and 0.285. The defence those rounds rested on held: this diagnosis's central reading is about WHICH leg is thinnest rather than about the rate, and a six-card leg makes it stronger. Two things the correction did NOT do, so nobody re-reads them as moved: no axis figure changes, and the death drains did not become inert — they gained a component and a rate, and this document now treats them as a second line rather than as a mis-declaration.

The two runs in sim/ are NOT a controlled A/B. They were separate invocations, the difference is -0.050 with ci95 [-0.299, +0.206] against a design MDE of 0.440, and only the 88bffd9b run describes v1.0.0: 4 wins of 20, win rate 0.20, ci95 [0.081, 0.416]. Every seat is Forge's AI on both sides, and the engine's own note is that the AI is 'best with aggro and midrange decks' — so for THIS deck the figure is closer to a measurement than the fleet's usual lower bound, and 0.25 sits inside the interval, so the run does not show the deck underperforming a four-seat baseline.

Nothing measures survival under opposing removal. The goldfish models no opponents and no wipes; the sim models opponents but plays our seat with an AI. The archenemy problem is measured on the pod's side (targeting.json) and unmeasured on ours.

engine.json was rewritten against v1.0.0 while this diagnosis was being written and its engine-critic pass has not returned, so its claims are cited here as un-attacked. Where it and this document overlap they agree — six removal spells, none answering a land; the payoff group mis-declared in both directions.

deck_recon.json is as_of 2026-08-03, three weeks before this baseline, and names cards the pilot has since cut (Cavern of Souls, Command Tower is still in). Only its inclusion percentages and posture quotes are leaned on, each dated in place.

bracket_report.json's freshness block records decklist_sha256: null, so the audit cannot confirm the bracket floor of 4 was computed against this exact list. A bare `bracket-check edgar-vampires` would settle it.

No candidate_pool.json exists for this deck. Adds come from the audit's closer search, a deterministic card-search over the corpus for the payoff trigger, and dated recon — not from a scored pool, so a better card may exist that nothing here would surface.

findings.note: ROUND 4, CLOSED. This was my only open finding (round 3, `over-claimed`): the entry dismissed a one-card single point of failure with 'stack 009 kills a three-seat pod', dropping the precondition that its own lean_into[0] states. The scoped fix closes it, and I checked it against the stack rather than against the quotation. Field by field: stack 009's scenario.board.you is exactly Purphoros, Impact Tremors, Warleader's Call, Anointed Procession and 'five lands' -- the entry names all four permanents and the five lands, and 'three payoffs and a doubler' is the right reading of them; all three opponents sit at life 12 with 'no instant-speed interaction held' -- the entry carries both; and final_state says 'EXACTLY lethal to a three-opponent pod at 12 life', 'Exactly lethal, zero margin' and 'the per-seat figure is 12 and the two are not interchangeable' -- the entry carries all three, including the 36-versus-12 warning. It is now MORE precise than lean_into[0], which is the right direction for the site where the claim is load-bearing. The volunteered cross-reference also holds: engine.json's open_questions[2] -- the third -- is exactly 'How many two-mana Vampire casts does the payoff suite need to take one seat from 40 to 0 with only ONE doubler on the battlefield?', and its why_it_matters opens 'Every verified damage figure in this model starts from a pod already below 15.' A second artifact, written independently, records the same limit, so the precondition is a known gap rather than an accommodation written to satisfy me.

ROUND 4, the question the coordinator asked me to decide: whether the precondition hollowed the argument out. It did not, and I judged it independently rather than taking the entry's word. What this entry has to establish is narrow -- that a one-card component is a declared ceiling on a bonus line rather than a defect in the deck -- and that needs exactly one thing: a win the deck reaches without the card. 'The payoff class closes a game with no infinite piece anywhere on the board' is precisely what stack 009 proves and is sufficient for that. What was given up -- 'kills a three-seat pod', read as from 40 -- was never proved and did no work the narrower claim cannot do. The heavier evidence for the same conclusion sits elsewhere in the document and is untouched: lean_into[1]'s 49.1% assembled for THE GO-WIDE KILL against 4.6% for the infinite. A 49.1% route beside a 4.6% route is what makes the infinite a bonus; stack 009 supplies the 'and it actually kills' half. I also tested the opposite conclusion the coordinator raised -- that the entry should now concede Conqueror matters more. It should not: Conqueror is a five-mana Vampire body that fires eminence and collects lords and is half of two checker-passed lines, and the entry neither denies that nor proposes cutting it; it already carries the log 001 fact that the table countered it. One residual I name rather than charge: 'which is the claim this entry needs' is the document certifying its own sufficiency. I agree with it on the reasoning above, but that clause is an assertion and not evidence.

ROUND 4, scope verified independently rather than trusted. The gate still passes with identical counts (16 axes, 2 weak, 4 cut / 4 add, 5 open questions); the sha is unchanged at 88bffd9b; `iterations` moved 2 -> 3, which is the revision counter and not a prose field; and my round-3 block is preserved byte-identical under `skeptic` (compared as parsed structures). Every field I quoted verbatim in round 3 is character-identical today: the verdict at 1,067 characters with the same opening and the same closing clause, lean_into[0] whole, axes[4]'s closing sentence, gaps[0]'s closing sentence, single_points_of_failure[1]'s opening, and the eight engine components with their counts and rates. The one field that differs from what I read in round 3 is single_points_of_failure[0].why, which grew from 372 characters to about a thousand. The scope assertion holds, and nothing was improved alongside the repair.

ROUND 3. The ranking is genuinely withdrawn, not deferred. Three tests. (i) The axis keeps its `weakness` verdict and -6, so nothing was downgraded to buy the retraction. (ii) All three round-2 supports are named and withdrawn, and I re-verified the source claims: goldfish.py's `_mana_pips` sums every {W|U|B|R|G|C} symbol as 1 and digits as their value, and the stated mulligan rule keeps 'hands with 2-5 lands' -- so neither the 91.3% nor the 80.1% can register a black screw, exactly as the entry says. (iii) The one colour-aware number the bench owns is quoted AGAINST the deck ('it points the other way: 82.2% on-curve black with rocks against Karsten's 90%'), which is what separates an honest gap from a deferral -- a deferral would have buried it. One imprecision I record rather than charge: 'a static hypergeometric that never meets the deck's curve' understates `manabase.achieved_probability`, which sets its turn from `earliest_turn` and `max_pips` (B: earliest 1, max_pips 3, effective_pips 2), so it is curve-informed at one representative turn rather than curve-blind. The conclusion is unaffected either way -- a static castability figure is not a games-lost rate and cannot be ranked against an assembly rate in either direction.

ROUND 3. The routing is honest and specific, which is what makes it a question rather than an excuse. It names the ranking as the thing being declined, names the missing measurement concretely -- 'how often is a black spell in hand, affordable by total mana, and uncastable for want of a black source' -- calls it 'a gap in the SIMULATOR rather than in this document', and carries `settled_by: goldfish`. That is a buildable specification, not a wish. It also states the consequence plainly: it 'decides whether the next slots go to the payoff leg or to the mana base', so a reader knows the prescription's ordering is the thing left open.

ROUND 3, the unprompted second site, verified. It now reads 'this says the mana COUNT works and says nothing about which colours those lands make' and names its own instrument. Correctly scoped: it keeps the figures, keeps the `strength` verdict (which is right -- 91.3% is a real land-drop result), and narrows only the inference. The log quote beside it is still verbatim in log 001.

ROUND 3. I looked for a THIRD site of the colour-blind conflation and did not find one. All four occurrences of 91.3% and both of 80.1%: the verdict (a quantity claim, 'every multi-card component turns over'), axes[0] (corrected), axes[4] (the correction itself), and axes[5] ramp -- where the land drop is the RIGHT instrument, because ramp is a quantity axis. Every other colour claim in the document is sourced to pips rather than to a goldfish figure, and I recomputed both: single_points_of_failure[1]'s 'hardest cast' rests on the 14-cards-with-two-or-more-pips enumeration with Bloodletter alone at three, and add_candidates[0]'s 'lightest load' on 11 red pips across 11 cards. The closest thing to a fourth site is the verdict's 'a castable Vampire in 92.3% of games' -- the goldfish measures DRAWN, not cast, and cannot see colour -- but 'castable' is a defined term from goldfish_targets' own note ('thirteen Vampire creatures at mana value <=2 ... the class you can cast alongside the rest of the plan'), so under its source's definition the sentence is accurate. Worth one word ('drawn') if the verdict is ever touched again; not a finding.

ROUND 3, the compression. Clause by clause against the round-2 verdict, nothing load-bearing left the document. The opening four figures are verbatim; 'what limits it is conversion under focus' is weakened to 'what I can measure end to end is conversion', which is the round-3 withdrawal doing its work rather than a loss; the payoff-leg sentence, the card-draw sentence and the kill figures all survive; and 'Black may be' is ADDED, so the reader of the verdict alone is now told there are two candidate limiters and only one is measurable. The single removal is the paired-difference paragraph, and both halves of it survive: the figure is intact in engine/components[3], which I re-read this round ('the sim does NOT show combat losing the exchange ... +8.60 with a 95% t-interval of [-15.26, +32.46]'), and the withdrawal is in gaps[0](a). A reader of the verdict alone no longer sees the self-correction -- but the verdict no longer makes the claim it corrected, so there is nothing left there to correct. 'Nothing lost' holds.

ROUND 3. The hypergeometrics are exact: 1 - C(97,7)/C(99,7) = 13.71% for two copies and 1 - C(98,7)/C(99,7) = 7.07% for one, which is the 13.7% -> 7.1% the entry states and the same 7.1% the corpus quotes for a named card. The costing is now real rather than annotated: it says in terms that the tracked 4.6% assembled and 2.8% by turn six 'are measured WITH Sanguine Bond in the group and do not describe the deck after this swap', that both halves become single cards, and that 'the post-swap rate is unmeasured' -- then routes it to open_questions[0], which now also asks the sandbox to run all four (add, natural_cut) pairs. My round-2 finding is closed. It still cross-references cut_candidates[3] rather than naming stacks 005 and 006 in place; the mechanical contract is met (orphans_stack sits on the cut entry, both stacks pass, 006 is live, and validate-diagnosis recomputes it) and the pointer is explicit, so I record this rather than charge it.

ROUND 3. The change record is complete against my round-2 finding: all three re-pointed citations are named with the row they left and the row they landed on (single_points_of_failure[0] and [1] off the effect-class row onto 'a named card is 7.1% of your opening seven'; lean_into[1] onto the tutors row), both rounds' withdrawals are listed, and round 3's own is the first thing in its paragraph. I re-verified all 22 citations in the revision are still verbatim after whitespace and (strategy:x.y) normalisation, and that each new row is the one its claim actually asserts. In-place corrections are not in the record -- axes[0]'s second site, Kambal's re-pricing -- but each is self-documented at its own site, which is the harder half to lose.

ROUND 3. Every stack-derived claim in the document checked against the stacks themselves for the first time, and all are faithful. Stack 009's final_state: 'NINE separate triggered abilities go on the stack, and the line is EXACTLY lethal to a three-opponent pod at 12 life ... Per opponent: 3x2 + 3x1 + 3x1 = 12 damage ... Exactly lethal, zero margin' -- lean_into[0]'s 'nine triggers, 12 to each seat, exactly lethal into a three-seat pod at 12 with zero margin' is faithful including the precondition. 'Stack 008 measures 10 per cast through two doublers' matches 008's '5 triggers x 2 = 10 damage to each opponent' through the verified 1->2->4 doubling. engine/components[1]'s 'Stack 010 proves the doublers stacking to eight tokens off one eminence trigger' matches 010's 'EIGHT 1/1 black Vampire tokens from the one trigger: 1 -> 2 -> 4 -> 8'. All three carry checker.verdict == pass, and no combo line anywhere in the document is stated as fact without one.

ROUND 3 hygiene. Gate passes (16 axes, 2 weak, 4 cut / 4 add, 5 open questions); `iterations: 2`; sha unchanged at 88bffd9b and still matching cards.json, goldfish_metrics.json and mana_analysis.json; every axes[].measured.value still equals deck-audit. My round-2 block is preserved byte-identical -- I compared the parsed structures. Nothing outside the four revised sites moved: cut_candidates, all eight engine components and their rates, single_points_of_failure, lean_into and the twelve unrevised axes are word for word what I read in round 2, so no correction was smuggled in beside a repair. All standing clearances re-confirmed by inspection where they were cheap to re-confirm and otherwise left alone as instructed.

ROUND 3 RECORD, kept verbatim so the file shows what was found and not only what closed. The finding as written then, status `over-claimed` at the time: ROUND 3, and this is ground no round has attacked: I read stacks 008, 009 and 010 themselves rather than the prose about them. The entry dismisses a one-card single point of failure with 'The deck does not need it, because stack 009 kills a three-seat pod with no infinite piece on the board' -- and stack 009's scenario board puts all three opponents at TWELVE life with 'no instant-speed interaction held', with Purphoros, Impact Tremors, Warleader's Call and Anointed Procession already on the battlefield. Its final_state says 'EXACTLY lethal to a three-opponent pod at 12 life ... Exactly lethal, zero margin' and insists 'the per-seat figure is 12 and the two are not interchangeable'. So the stack proves the last 12 points of a 40-point clock off a four-permanent board, and the entry compresses that into 'kills a three-seat pod', which reads as 'wins the game' and is what carries the dismissal of Bloodthirsty Conqueror. lean_into[0] states the same stack correctly -- 'exactly lethal into a three-seat pod at 12 with zero margin' -- and axes[10] says '12 to each seat', so the document knows the precondition and drops it at the one site where it is load-bearing. This is the radagast 36-into-40 lesson, one deck over. Fix by carrying lean_into[0]'s clause into this entry; the argument may well survive it, but it has to be made against the real board.
